title: Decide the HumbleStudio standalone, module, or absorption path
summary: Run a reversible evidence-backed platform-role pilot for HumbleStudio instead of assuming that overlap requires a merger.
acceptance_criteria: Evaluate the current standalone and fusion posture: Likely destination for selected Architect capabilities; Board and design editing remain its core.
Inventory unique, duplicated, shared, and obsolete capabilities with evidence.
Define the user mental model and navigation impact of standalone, companion, module, and absorption alternatives.
Map data ownership, permissions, credentials, filesystems, network, and destructive operations for every alternative.
Measure code duplication, performance, test burden, release cadence, support burden, and failure blast radius.
Choose one reversible pilot smaller than a full merger.
Define exact module API, host boundary, source ownership, and fallback to standalone operation.
Preserve repository-qualified identity and evidence lineage during the pilot.
Do not move private or destructive domain ownership into HumbleControl merely for convenience.
Define migration, rollback, uninstall, and data-export posture before the pilot starts.
Define success, failure, stop, and reconsideration criteria.
Run the pilot with representative workflows and performance evidence.
Collect product and operator feedback without implying a final merger decision.
Compare the pilot with the standalone baseline.
Issue an explicit decision: remain separate, share library, embed module, absorb, or retire.
Any irreversible next step requires a new repo-owned ticket and Jan approval.
Update the portfolio fusion map and each affected repository charter.
Keep public Website and private product boundaries intact.
Validate the decision artifact and all affected contracts.
Finish the pilot without app-owned warnings.

blocked_by.reason: The capstone scope depends on reviewed earlier-wave foundations.

agent_notes: Portfolio Capstone and Operating System Wave 10.
Non-scope: do not release, deploy, merge products, mutate external data, delete, restore, or enable monetization from this planning ticket.
Alternative considered and rejected: adding more disconnected ambitious features without charter, capacity, assurance, and product evidence would make the portfolio less trustworthy.
Wave 10 is a realization and rationalization layer, not a reason to keep expanding the backlog indefinitely.
Current fusion posture: Likely destination for selected Architect capabilities; Board and design editing remain its core..
Wave 11 execution reconciliation: `required-prerequisite`. Use the Wave 11 implementation program as the delivery entry point while preserving this ticket's evidence and intent.

Wave 12 deep reassessment: decision `retain-charter-input`, relevance `next`, current priority `medium`, execution gate `use as governing context, not another parallel backlog`. Portfolio and product charters remain decision inputs, while Wave 11 and Wave 12 own implementation and completion.
Wave 13 human-validation reassessment: `retain-product-charter-input` / `next` / priority `high`. Product role, lifecycle, and investment decisions frame the validation program.

Final Wave 14 validity review: `valid`; publication `publish-after-fresh-reconciliation`; implementation sequence `after-sudoku`. Product role, lifecycle, and investment decisions frame the validation program.
